## Install

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("tenmeh/unsaved")
```

## Track your form

List the input ids that belong to the form. Add `unsaved_badge()` to show
the number of changed fields. A changed field also gets a dot by its label.

```r
library(shiny)
library(unsaved)

ui <- fluidPage(
  unsaved_badge(),
  tabsetPanel(
    id = "tabs",
    tabPanel("Profile", textInput("name", "Name", "Ada"),
             actionButton("save", "Save"),
             actionButton("discard", "Discard")),
    tabPanel("Other", "Another page")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Replace this in-memory store with your app's save code.
  saved_name <- reactiveVal("Ada")
  save_record <- function() {
    saved_name(input$name)
  }
  tracker <- unsaved_track("name", on_save = save_record)
  observeEvent(input$save, {
    save_record()
    tracker$mark_saved()
  })
  observeEvent(input$discard, tracker$discard())
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

The package does not save data. Call `mark_saved()` after your own save
finishes. Call `discard()` to restore the saved input values.

`changed()` gives the ids of changed fields, `count()` gives their number,
and `is_dirty()` tells you whether there are changes. Use `baseline()` for
the saved values. The first value of a field added by `renderUI()` after
start joins the baseline automatically.

## Save and leave

An `on_save` function adds **Save and leave** to the navigation dialog.
It takes no arguments. The tracker marks values saved after it returns
successfully, then opens the requested tab. Returning `FALSE` or raising
an error keeps the edits and shows a safe failure message.

## The navigation guard

The guard stops tab clicks, arrow keys and `updateTabsetPanel()` while the
form is dirty. The user can keep editing, discard, or save and leave.
Call `mark_saved()`, `discard()` (and wait for the restored inputs), or
`pause()` before navigating from the server. `resume()` restarts tracking.
Set `guard_nav = FALSE` to turn off the navigation guard.

The close or refresh guard uses the browser's own warning. Browsers may
suppress it, especially without prior interaction. Set `guard_unload = FALSE`
to turn it off. The live demo runs in an iframe; open it in a new tab to
try the browser warning.

[Try the profile editor](live-demo.html).

## Field labels and the change list

Give `inputs` names for the labels shown in a review screen:

```r
tracker <- unsaved_track(c("Full name" = "name", Role = "role"))
output$changes <- renderTable(tracker$diff()[, c("label", "change")])
```

`diff()` is reactive. It returns `name`, `label`, `change`, `saved` and
`current`, in input order. The values are list columns. Empty names use the
id, and duplicate ids are an error. Password fields are never tracked, so
their values cannot enter a snapshot, browser cache or change summary.
A reported password id stays excluded even after its widget is removed.

## Choose text and comparison rules

```r
tracker <- unsaved_track("name",
  text = unsaved_text(title = "Profile changes", keep = "Stay"),
  compare = list(name = unsaved_compare_text()),
  on_discard = function() showNotification("Changes discarded")
)
```

`unsaved_text()` controls the title, message, button text, saving text,
failure message and screen-reader text. `{n}` and `{s}` are message
placeholders. A dialog shared by several trackers uses the first one's text.
`unsaved_compare_text()` trims outer whitespace and treats empty text as
NULL; either rule can be turned off. A comparison can be NULL, one function
for every input, or a named list by input id. Each function takes saved and
current values and returns one non-missing logical for equality.

`on_discard()` runs after every server or dialog discard. Errors become
warnings. After a direct `discard()` call, inputs may not yet have returned
from the browser; use `baseline()` for saved values.

## Protect loading and other actions

```r
observeEvent(input$load, {
  record_id <- input$record
  tracker$confirm(function() load_record(record_id))
})
```

Clean or paused trackers run the action at once. Dirty trackers open the
dialog. Keep editing cancels. Discard restores, calls `on_discard`, then
runs the action once. Save and leave runs it only after a successful save.
Only one confirmation per tracker can be pending. Calling `confirm()` again
while waiting warns and drops the new action without running or queuing it.
The first confirmation stays open. Explicit confirmation works even with
`guard_nav = FALSE`.

For browser clicks, wrap a tag in `unsaved_guard()`, or add the
`data-unsaved-guard` attribute yourself:

```r
unsaved_guard(actionButton("delete", "Delete draft"))
unsaved_guard(tags$a(href = "/another-page", "Another page"))
```

Modal close buttons can use the same attribute. Dirty trackers with
`guard_nav = TRUE` block the click; discard or a successful save replays it.

## Modules

Create the tracker inside `moduleServer()` with local input ids. Do not
prefix them with `session$ns()`. Save, discard and navigation events stay
in that module. A badge counts distinct changed fields across modules.

## Use with rewind

`rewind` is an optional package for undo and redo:

```r
rewind::rewind_enable(inputs = "name")
tracker <- unsaved_track("name")
observeEvent(input$undo, rewind::rewind_undo())
observeEvent(input$redo, rewind::rewind_redo())
```

Undoing to saved values clears dirty state. Redo makes the form dirty again.
Discard is a normal edit, so rewind can undo it. For text, slow typing makes
several history steps; `updateOn = "blur"` gives one per edit. Ctrl+Z inside
a text box uses the browser's own undo, so use rewind's controls or API.
